item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0014-E001","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0014-E002","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0014-E003","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Coordinated progovernment online networks reportedly spread narratives and smear campaigns against López Obrador's perceived rivals. In March 2023, pro-López Obrador accounts disseminated more than 20,000 tweets using unsubstantiated accusations linking Supreme Court president Norma Piña to drug trafficking; a later investigation identified the Red Brolan network spreading progovernment narratives and manipulated or unsubstantiated attacks on opponents and critical journalists, although no evidence showed government or party financing.","notes":["Narrowed “messages” to the excerpt’s “tweets.”"]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0014-E004","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0014-E005","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0014-E006","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0014-E007","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Mexico's telecommunications law required providers to retain metadata for two years and provide real-time geolocation or communications data to authorities under specified conditions. Between 2021 and 2023, Telcel reportedly supplied records of more than a dozen public officials in response to at least 14 Mexico City prosecutor orders without the required judicial authorization. INAI also lacked a quorum from March 2023, although the Supreme Court later allowed it to operate with four commissioners.","notes":["Narrowed the Telcel event from occurring specifically in 2023 to the excerpt’s 2021–2023 period."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0014-E008","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0014-E009","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0014-E010","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0014-E011","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0014-E012","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0014-E013","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0014-E014","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The World Bank reported a cautious countercyclical fiscal response, increased health and social-assistance spending, and public investment, while noting substantial support to loss-making PEMEX: cumulative government support of 2.7 percent of 2021 GDP during 2019–2021, with PEMEX debt of about MXN 2.243 trillion at end-2021. The 2022 budget aimed to stabilize debt and deficits; PEMEX continued to report losses and high financial obligations and remained dependent on substantial government support.","notes":["Replaced the unsupported characterization that revenue-stabilization funds were “heavily depleted” and that PEMEX was explicitly described as a “fiscal risk.”"]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0014-E015","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The government enacted a simplified income-tax regime for MSMEs and self-employed workers, adding tax-authority tools against evasion and reducing filing procedures. The reform was designed to be revenue-neutral in the short term and was expected to increase formalization over the medium to long term. The operation also supported remote bank-account opening for Mexican migrants and expansion of financial services through electronic payment systems.","notes":["Removed unsupported claims about neutral poverty and social effects, consumer protection, and cybersecurity."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0014-E016","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0014-E017","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0014-E018","status":"rejected","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The exact excerpt concerns budget transparency, procurement, auditing, monitoring, and general risks; it does not support the proposed disaster-budget assessment or risk-financing claims."]}]}
